method: Bounded original mapped x86-64 disassembly with VA = 0x140000000 + file offset. No runtime experiment.
findings: At 0x1422c141a this branch reloads argument4 from RBP+0x7f into R14, then calls the known collection append helper for argument4+0xa8.

0x1422c1472 compares the collection count at argument4+0xb0 against EDI, initialized to zero at 0x1422c04d9 and not reassigned before this comparison. Nonzero count jumps directly to cleanup at 0x1422c15b1.
Zero count copies a 165-TCHAR message from 0x14610b980. Its text is not reproduced. If severity gate 0x1480dffb0 is at least 2, 0x1422c14ff logs it with severity2 via 0x142c54b70.

The zero-count branch also calls 0x142c26df0 and 0x142ca0060 with the copied message, then calls previously identified platform exit-request helper 0x142ce8ac0 at 0x1422c159f with ECX=0. Exact presentation effects of those two earlier helpers remain unresolved.

The paired successful command-line override branch does not pass this count guard: cleanup at 0x1422c06de/0x1422c06e4 jumps to 0x1422c15b1/0x1422c15ac. Applying this guard universally after paired overrides would change original control flow.
limitations: This proves the selected branch only, not complete fallback precedence, literal contents, host assignments, actual process termination or runtime behavior.
No native guard is installed; presentation helpers and all incoming branches require further recovery.
